steps.name: CreateScaleCube
steps.label: Create Scale Cube
steps.goal: Stand a box the height of the asset, as its registry entry states it, beside the origin - the modeller's real-world ruler. The box is measured back afterwards, because a Max scene left on the factory inch builds one of the right number and the wrong size.
steps.pass_criteria: A box named SCALE_REF_{n}cm exists at the asset's height.
steps.fail_criteria: No box is created, or Max measures it at a height other than the one asked for - which means the scene is not on the studio unit.
steps.min_scenario: You hand-build the structure to the studio's convention - when the convention is clear and the inputs are present.
steps.max_scenario: The convention is undocumented or inconsistent across artists; you rebuild and reconcile it by hand.

steps.name: ImportDesignViews
steps.label: Import Design Views
steps.goal: Stand the design's T-pose front - the image the design mesh was generated from - up as a reference plane behind the model, plus the back T-pose when the design published one. Planes come in non-renderable and frozen, so they cannot be dragged by accident while orbiting.
steps.pass_criteria: At minimum the front reference plane is in the scene, or the step reports that there is no design publish to take one from.
steps.fail_criteria: A design publish names view images that are not on disk.
steps.min_scenario: Published dsn with a front view - one lookup, one import.
steps.max_scenario: No dsn publish or missing view images; manual hunt required.

steps.name: ConvertDesignModel
steps.label: Convert Design Model for Max
steps.goal: THE ONE STEP THE BLENDER RECIPE DOES NOT HAVE. Blender reads the design publish's .glb directly; 3ds Max has no glTF importer at all. Rather than install a third-party glTF plugin machine-wide on every workstation and farm node, the pipeline converts ahead of the import: the mesh service (headless Blender) writes a .fbx beside this version's .max, and Max imports that. FBX and not OBJ because FBX declares its own axis and unit metadata, which Max's importer honours, where OBJ carries none and Max applies its own flip-YZ preset with nothing in the file to arbitrate.
steps.pass_criteria: A .fbx sits beside the version's .max and the service verified its extents against the source .glb.
steps.fail_criteria: The conversion failed, or the written .fbx does not measure the same as the .glb it came from.
steps.min_scenario: The service converts and verifies in a few seconds, or reuses the .fbx a previous run left.
steps.max_scenario: A design mesh Blender's exporter chokes on; you convert it by hand and check its orientation in Max yourself.

steps.name: ImportDesignModel
steps.label: Import Design Model
steps.goal: Import the converted design mesh, name it {asset}_dsn, and file it into a hidden DSN layer as a read-only design artifact - the UV and silhouette source for the steps that follow, never the hero mesh. A multi-part design mesh is attached into one, because retopology and UV transfer are single-object modifiers and would otherwise see one piece and ignore the rest. Prior design artifacts and prior proxies are purged first, so a re-run leaves the same scene as the first run.
steps.pass_criteria: One mesh named {asset}_dsn is in the scene, hidden in the DSN layer, and recorded in shared_data.
steps.fail_criteria: The import brought in no geometry, or the converted file is missing.
steps.min_scenario: Published dsn with a mesh - one lookup, one import.
steps.max_scenario: No dsn publish or an unreadable mesh; manual setup required.

steps.name: CreateProxyModel
steps.label: Create Proxy Model
steps.goal: Throw away the design mesh's topology and keep its surface: retopologise it to a face budget, producing the clean mostly-quad proxy that becomes the hero asset once it has the design's UVs. Where the Blender leg needs two ops - voxel remesh then decimate - Max's Retopology modifier does both at once, so decimating after it would only re-introduce the triangle soup it just removed. The budget is a FACE TARGET rather than Blender's derived voxel size, because a face target is scale-invariant: the same number gives the same relative density on a 20cm prop and a 6m set. REQUIRES A VIEWPORT: Max's Retopology compute is driven from the modify panel, so this step needs a GUI Max session - requires_display is set, and the runner launches the UI for it exactly as the Unreal and Blender legs already do for their viewport steps (#3845).
steps.pass_criteria: A proxy named {asset}_{task} exists with materially fewer faces than the design mesh.
steps.fail_criteria: No design mesh in the scene, or Retopology did not run - which in Max is a silent no-op unless the op checks for it, so the op measures the result and raises instead.
steps.min_scenario: Clean design mesh - Retopology produces usable topology at the target automatically.
steps.max_scenario: A self-intersecting or non-manifold design mesh; you retopologise the awkward regions by hand after the automated pass.

steps.name: TransferUVsToLo
steps.label: Transfer UVs to Proxy
steps.goal: Sample the design mesh's UVs onto the clean proxy across different topology, so the design's generated textures still fit - without this the proxy would have to be unwrapped and re-textured from scratch. Max's equivalent of Blender's DATA_TRANSFER is the Attribute_Transfer modifier, NEW IN 3DS MAX 2027; there is no equivalent on an earlier Max and the op says so by name rather than degrading. Runs before PlaceGeometry so the two meshes are still co-located and the spatial lookup is over coincident surfaces.
steps.pass_criteria: The proxy carries map channel 1 and it is per-face-corner - more map vertices than geometry vertices, i.e. UV seams survived rather than collapsing to one UV per vertex.
steps.fail_criteria: Either mesh is missing, the modifier is absent (a Max older than 2027), or the proxy ends up with no map channel or a collapsed per-vertex one.
steps.min_scenario: A proxy retopologised from the source it is sampling - the projection lands on the same surface it came from.
steps.max_scenario: Topology too different for the projection to be trusted; manual UV unwrap after the automated pass. Note that Attribute_Transfer has no max-distance parameter, so a far-deviating proxy samples something rather than nothing.

steps.name: PlaceGeometry
steps.label: Place Geometry
steps.goal: Scale the proxy to the asset's canonical height and ground it at Z=0, then measure it back - a rig reads limb lengths off the mesh, a layout drops it onto a floor and a camera frames it by height, and all three are quietly wrong if the model ships at whatever scale the design service produced. Runs after the UV transfer so the transfer had two co-located meshes to work with.
steps.pass_criteria: The proxy measures the asset's height to within 0.05cm and its lowest point is Z=0.
steps.fail_criteria: The proxy is missing, or it measures something other than what was asked for.

steps.name: EnsureModelGroup
steps.label: Ensure Model Group
steps.goal: File the hero mesh under the cross-DCC mdl/hi grouping - Point helpers in Max, where Maya uses transform groups and Blender uses Empties, all answering mdl.query.members the same way - bake the placement scale into the vertices so the publish does not ship a node scale, keep the design artifact hidden in its layer, and save the scene.
steps.pass_criteria: mdl/hi exists, the proxy is a member of it, and the .max is saved.
steps.fail_criteria: The grouping could not be created, the proxy did not end up in it, or the scene could not be saved.

steps.name: EnsureTurntable
steps.label: Ensure Turntable
steps.goal: Guarantee the scene carries exactly one turntable rig - a spin handle the model hangs off and a camera framed on what it sweeps - lit by the HDRI library's default environment, and save it, so the rig is in the version an artist opens and the publish's CleanTt has something real to strip.
steps.pass_criteria: A turntable handle and camera exist, the model is parented under the handle, and the scene environment is an HDRI that is actually in use.
steps.fail_criteria: There is no model to spin, the HDRI library resolved nothing, or the environment did not take.
steps.min_scenario: You build the orbit and drop in a studio HDRI by hand, having done it enough times to remember every setting.
steps.max_scenario: You hand-build a key light instead, it loses a fight with the environment, and the review render comes back a black silhouette - which nobody notices until the review.

steps.name: SetRenderSettings
steps.label: Set Render Settings
steps.goal: Pin the render to a cheap clay review pass - PNG at 1280x720, Arnold, over the SCENE's own frame range - so what comes out is judged on form and is identical from one run to the next.
steps.pass_criteria: The scene reads back the requested range, size and format, and the clay override is on.
steps.fail_criteria: The scene's frame range is empty or backwards, the renderer is not available, or the settings did not take.
steps.min_scenario: You set the output size, format and range by hand and happen to get all four right.
steps.max_scenario: One setting is off - EXR instead of PNG, eight frames instead of the turntable, the scene's leftover renderer - and the whole render has to be done again.

steps.name: Playblast
steps.label: Playblast
steps.goal: Render the turntable camera over the scene's frame range into the version's render dir as a PNG sequence named the way the rest of the pipeline reads sequences.
steps.pass_criteria: Every frame in the range exists on disk under the version's sequence path.
steps.fail_criteria: There is no turntable camera to render, or a frame is missing.
steps.min_scenario: You kick off the render to a folder you picked, and it lands where you meant it to.
steps.max_scenario: The frames go somewhere the pipeline cannot see, or come out named Max's way rather than the studio's, and every surface downstream reports the version as having no media.

steps.name: ProcessRenders
steps.label: Process Renders
steps.goal: Encode the rendered turntable into the version's review mp4 and cut a still thumbnail from the middle of it, at the .preview/.thumb paths every review surface derives from the coordinate.
steps.pass_criteria: An mp4 exists at the version's preview path and a thumbnail at its thumb path.
steps.fail_criteria: There are no frames to encode, or the encode produced nothing.
steps.min_scenario: You drop the frames into a player, export a quicktime and grab a still for the card.
steps.max_scenario: The review media never gets made, so the work exists only as a folder of frames nobody outside the room can open.

steps.name: CleanTt
steps.label: Clean Turntable
steps.goal: Guarantee the published model is not a child of review furniture - reparent anything hanging off a turntable handle back to world (world transform preserved), delete the turntable cameras and the handle, and drop the turntable layer if it is left empty.
steps.pass_criteria: No turntable handle or turntable camera remains in the scene.
steps.fail_criteria: A turntable rig is present and could not be removed.
steps.min_scenario: You do the cleanup by hand before handing off - quick when you remember it.
steps.max_scenario: You forget or do it wrong; the mistake ships in the file and gets flagged downstream, forcing a redo.

steps.name: PivotsToOrigin
steps.label: Pivots To Origin
steps.goal: Guarantee the canonical mdl/{lod} handle hierarchy exists with the model inside it, and move its pivot - and its descendants' pivots - to the world origin, so every downstream consumer places the asset the same way.
steps.pass_criteria: The mdl handle exists, holds the model geometry, and its pivot is at the world origin.
steps.fail_criteria: The group could not be built, or holds no geometry to publish.
steps.min_scenario: You do the cleanup by hand before handing off - quick when you remember it.
steps.max_scenario: You forget or do it wrong; the mistake ships in the file and gets flagged downstream, forcing a redo.

steps.name: DeleteHistory
steps.label: Delete History
steps.goal: Bake every modifier on the model into its geometry, so the published asset is a finished mesh rather than a live recipe a downstream artist can change the shape of by deleting an entry.
steps.pass_criteria: No node under the mdl handle carries a modifier stack.
steps.fail_criteria: A stack could not be collapsed.
steps.min_scenario: You do the cleanup by hand before handing off - quick when you remember it.
steps.max_scenario: You forget or do it wrong; the mistake ships in the file and gets flagged downstream, forcing a redo.

steps.name: FreezeTransformations
steps.label: Freeze Transformations
steps.goal: Bake any rotation or scale on the model into its vertex data so the published geometry is correct at node identity, and no downstream importer can disagree about its size.
steps.pass_criteria: The mdl handle and its geometry descendants carry no residual rotation or scale.
steps.fail_criteria: The transform could not be baked.
steps.min_scenario: You do the cleanup by hand before handing off - quick when you remember it.
steps.max_scenario: You forget or do it wrong; the mistake ships in the file and gets flagged downstream, forcing a redo.

steps.name: EnsureMaterialGroups
steps.label: Ensure Material Groups
steps.goal: Guarantee the model carries the {material}_mtl grouping convention the texture, lookdev and MSD contracts bind to - wrapping a groupless mesh in a default_mtl group with a clay material rather than publishing an asset no downstream task can key off.
steps.pass_criteria: Every model mesh sits under a *_mtl group and wears the matching material.
steps.fail_criteria: There is no LOD bucket to group under, or no geometry to group.
steps.min_scenario: A generated model carries a clean default_mtl/clay placeholder and flows through the rest of the pipeline unchanged.
steps.max_scenario: A groupless model breaks Substance texture-set boundaries and the lighting attach downstream.

steps.name: SaveScene
steps.label: Save Scene
steps.goal: Save the cleaned .max in place, so the version on disk is the scene the publish is about to export from - and so the whole-file .max delivery is a real, current file rather than whatever was last written.
steps.pass_criteria: 3ds Max saved the session to its current file.
steps.fail_criteria: The session has no file to save to, or Max refused to write it.
steps.min_scenario: You do the cleanup by hand before handing off - quick when you remember it.
steps.max_scenario: You forget or do it wrong; the mistake ships in the file and gets flagged downstream, forcing a redo.

steps.name: ExportModelFileFormats
steps.label: Export Model File Formats
steps.goal: Emit the model group into the version's render dir in every format this Max install can natively write, plus the whole-file .max, so consumers that will never open 3ds Max can read the asset.
steps.pass_criteria: A file exists in the version's render dir for every format in EXPORT_FORMATS.
steps.fail_criteria: An exporter is missing or raised, or a named format wrote no file.
steps.min_scenario: You hand-export the file(s) to the right place in the right format(s), double-checking the path - when you remember every format and where it goes.
steps.max_scenario: A format's missing, the path's wrong, or settings are off; downstream can't find or use it, pings you, and you re-export - days of back-and-forth.

steps.name: ConvertModelToGlb
steps.label: Convert Model To Glb
steps.goal: Deliver the .glb the model contract names and 3ds Max cannot write, by converting the exported .fbx through the mesh service - so a Max model publish carries the same format set as a Blender one, with the Z-up to Y-up rotation performed and RECORDED in one place rather than assumed at both ends.
steps.pass_criteria: A .glb exists beside the other exports and the service verified its extents against the .fbx it was made from.
steps.fail_criteria: The .fbx is missing, the conversion raised, or the written .glb does not measure the same as its source.
steps.min_scenario: You round-trip the model through another package by hand to get a .glb, and it happens to come out the right way up.
steps.max_scenario: The axis flip is applied twice or not at all; the asset arrives on its face in the viewer, and nobody can tell whether the model, the exporter or the importer is wrong.

steps.name: GenerateSceneDescription
steps.label: Generate Scene Description
steps.goal: Serialise the model scene - geometry, materials and their assignments - into the cross-DCC MSD payload and persist it onto the version manifest's data field, which is the only part of the manifest that survives to publish/latest and the only place downstream tasks can read the material-to-geometry map from.
steps.pass_criteria: The version .msd carries a scene description with at least one geometry entry.
steps.fail_criteria: The description could not be generated, or could not be committed to the version manifest.
steps.min_scenario: Someone hand-enters the notes/metadata for the records - quick when they bother.
steps.max_scenario: It's left blank; downstream has no context for what changed and has to ask around or guess.

steps.name: AddDescription
steps.label: Add Description
steps.goal: Guarantee the publish carries a description, taken from whatever triggered it or composed from the coordinate - never from a dialog, because this recipe has to survive a farm run where there is nobody to answer one.
steps.pass_criteria: A non-empty description is in shared_data for Publish to consume.
steps.fail_criteria: None - this step cannot fail; it either finds a description or writes one.
steps.min_scenario: Someone hand-enters the notes/metadata for the records - quick when they bother.
steps.max_scenario: It's left blank; downstream has no context for what changed and has to ask around or guess.

steps.name: Publish
steps.label: Publish
steps.goal: Cut the next major version, copy it to publish/latest with its exported formats and its scene description, move the downstream tasks to ready and mirror the publish to the tracker - so the rest of the pipeline can consume this model by a stable address instead of by knowing which artist version was good.
steps.pass_criteria: publish/latest holds the published files and the version msd.
steps.fail_criteria: The publish raised, or there was no coordinate to publish.
steps.min_scenario: You manually copy the version to the publish/latest location and a coordinator hand-updates the tracker and pings downstream - when everyone actually does their part.
steps.max_scenario: The coordinator's slammed and forgets (or no one notifies downstream); everyone waiting burns days on Slack, text, email, phone, and walking the building to find out if it's ready.

steps.name: CreateFolders
steps.label: Create Folders
steps.goal: Create a working folder in compliance with the studio's folder structure.
steps.end_result: Every time someone starts a task, the correct structure is created instantly - consistent and visible to the entire production.
steps.min_scenario: You hand-build the structure to the studio's convention — when the convention is clear and the inputs are present.
steps.max_scenario: The convention is undocumented or inconsistent across artists; you rebuild and reconcile it by hand.

steps.name: CopyDefaultFiles
steps.label: Copy Default Files
steps.goal: Copy the default file built by the studio for this task so that work can start with all available templates and setttings.
steps.end_result: Every time someone starts a task they start with a production tested default file.
steps.min_scenario: You hand-build the structure to the studio's convention — when the convention is clear and the inputs are present.
steps.max_scenario: The convention is undocumented or inconsistent across artists; you rebuild and reconcile it by hand.
